title: Welcome to the COSY Editorial & Learning Corner
dek: Welcome to our editorial room! Explore personal journal notes, language learning philosophies, and canonical curriculum guides across all 14 COSY target languages.

blocks.text: Welcome to **COSYmagazine**, the editorial corner of COSY Languages, a free site for learning 14 languages. Think of it as the notebook that sits next to the lessons: a place for ideas, stories, grammar curiosities and gentle advice for anyone learning a language. I'm JY DM, the founder of COSY, and I'm glad you are here.
blocks.say: Welcome to COSYmagazine, the editorial corner of COSY Languages, a free site for learning 14 languages. Think of it as the notebook that sits next to the lessons: a place for ideas, stories, grammar curiosities and gentle advice for anyone learning a language. I'm JY DM, the founder of COSY, and I'm glad you are here.

blocks.text: Everything on COSY is built around one belief: <mark class="hl-handwritten">speaking-first, immersion-based learning</mark>. You do not need to memorise abstract tables before you are allowed to talk. You connect with real people and say real things from day one, and the grammar follows. The magazine is where we think about that out loud.

blocks.text: COSYmagazine is published in **issues**, one for each month, each with its own theme. Inside an issue, articles are grouped into **desks**, a bit like sections in a newspaper:
blocks.say: COSYmagazine is published in issues, one for each month, each with its own theme. Inside an issue, articles are grouped into desks, a bit like sections in a newspaper:

items: **Front Page:** editorials, introductions and the big ideas behind COSY.
**Words:** vocabulary, phrases and ways to say things more naturally.
**Grammar:** clear, friendly explanations and rules worth knowing.
**COSYtalks:** longer conversations about learning, the mind and teaching.
**Saturday Mistakes:** common errors, with a corrected sentence and a quick quiz.
**Podcast:** the articles as listening, for walks, buses and washing-up.

blocks.text: Not everybody likes to read the same way, so each article can be opened in several modes.
blocks.say: Not everybody likes to read the same way, so each article can be opened in several modes.

items: **3D magazine spread:** the default. Pages turn like a real magazine, with the handwritten notes in the margins.
**Flat scroll:** a simple, calm, one-column page, ideal for phones.
**Presentation mode:** add `?stage=1` to an article's address and it plays block by block, perfect for a class screen.
**Teleprompter:** add `?script=1` and you get the spoken script in large type, handy if you want to read an article aloud or record your own version.

blocks.text: The magazine is one part of a small family of free tools. **COSYpractice** is where you do the speaking, listening and reading exercises. **COSYtools** is a set of helpers for learners and teachers. Whenever an article mentions a phrase or a rule, you will usually find a link so you can try it straight away.

blocks.text: Our year follows the shape of a school year, with a few extra surprises:
blocks.say: Our year follows the shape of a school year, with a few extra surprises:

items: **August: Get ready for school.** A fresh start. We talk about why speaking comes first, how the COSY curriculum is built, and how to begin a new language without fear.
**September: Me vs Intermediate Plateau.** For learners who feel stuck at B1: phrase upgrades, stronger adjectives and more precise verbs.
**October: JY DM's birthday & His favs.** A personal issue with my favourite grammar rules, words and ideas, together with Saturday Mistakes.
**November: November Academia.** Dark evenings, libraries and big questions: how the brain learns, and how play helps it.

blocks.title: Culture bite: why a magazine?
blocks.content: The word *magazine* comes from an Arabic word for a storehouse, and the idea of a publication as a storehouse of many different things passed into French and then English. That is exactly what we want here: a store of small, useful ideas that you can browse in any order, dip into for five minutes and come back to whenever you like.

blocks.question: What does adding ?stage=1 to an article address do?
options: Opens the article in presentation mode
Switches to the flat scroll layout
blocks.explanation: ?stage=1 plays the article block by block in presentation mode. ?script=1 shows the teleprompter script instead.

blocks.text: Pick an issue, pick a desk, pick the way you like to read. And when something sparks an idea, say it out loud in the language you are learning. That is the whole method, really.
